close_reason: Closed the jmap-types-scoped part of this finding: (1) Filter<T> rustdoc now carries an explicit 'Malformed-operator hazard' section documenting the silent-fallthrough behavior + server-side defenses; (2) regression test filter_with_typoed_operator_silently_decodes_as_match_all_condition in crate-jmap-types/src/query.rs pins the current decode behavior with two typo variants ('opperator', 'Operator'). The bead's candidate (a) tagged-discriminator is wire-incompatible with RFC 8620 §5.5 and was rejected. Candidate (b) server-side rejection of all-None Condition lives in server crates, NOT jmap-types — tracked as follow-up bd:JMAP-6azm with workspace-wide propagation guidance.
description: Pre-existing latent issue surfaced (NOT introduced) by the filter-algebra exclusion doc-sweep (commits fad2d24, c0ddb93). `Filter<T>` is #[serde(untagged)]; it tries `FilterOperator<T>` first (requires literal field "operator" + "conditions"), then falls through to `Condition(T)`. If a client sends a malformed operator clause — e.g. "Operator" capitalized incorrectly, or "operator" mis-typed as "operatr" — FilterOperator deserialization fails because the operator field is missing. Serde then tries Condition(T). T = EmailFilterCondition (and every other downstream FilterCondition) is a struct of all-optional fields with no #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]; explicitly documented in jmap-mail-types/src/query.rs:32 (\"Do not add #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] — it breaks #[serde(untagged)] deserialization\"). So the malformed clause silently deserializes to Filter::Condition(EmailFilterCondition::default()) which matches EVERY record. The new doc-comments correctly identify the hazard, but the hazard is realized RIGHT NOW even before extras: just send a clause with no operator key and a typo'd condition. No test covers this. Trigger: any caller sending a malformed operator. Bad behavior: query returns all records, no error. Fix candidates: (a) replace the untagged enum with a tagged discriminator (would be wire-incompatible), (b) reject the empty/all-None Condition case at the server, (c) add a doc warning telling SERVERS to verify Condition::is_all_none() and reject, (d) document the failure mode explicitly so server authors know to defend. Probe needed: write a test that sends `{"opperator":"AND","conditions":[]}` against an Email/query and asserts the deserializer rejects it OR documents it matches all.
title: Filter<T> deserialization silently maps malformed FilterOperator to FilterCondition
